newsitem.title: USA: ADM names G. Allen Andreas president.
newsitem.headline: ADM names G. Allen Andreas president.

text.p: Archer Daniels Midland Co said Monday it named G. Allen Andreas, nephew of chairman Dwayne Andreas, as president. Allen Andreas was recently named chief executive officer.
As president, he replaces James Randall, who will retire after 29 years of service. Randall has been president for more than 22 years.
The management changes will be effective July 1.

During Randall's tenure, ADM said, the company grew to more than $13.3 billion in revenues from $1.8 billion. Randall has been the principal operating officer of the company and directly supervised the construction, engineering and operation of ADM's 210 processing plants around the world.

"He has played the major role in building ADM's global operating network of processing plants and storage facilities linked by unparalleled worldwide communication and transportation systems," Dwayne Andreas said in a statement.

Other senior executive appointments include Charles Bayless as executive vice president, overseeing the worldwide processing operations of the company. He has been group vice president of ADM and president of the oilseed processing division.
Burnell Kraft was named senior vice president, continuing to supervise the global grain trade and merchandising operations.

Richard Reising will become senior vice president with management responsibility for certain executive and administrative functions. David Smith was named vice president, secretary and general counsel, replacing Reising. Smith had been assistant general counsel since 1995.
In April, Allen Andreas, 53, was named as chief executive officer of the agribusiness giant.

That move drew some criticism from some institutional shareholders since Allen Andreas' uncle, Dwayne Andreas, remains chairman. Institutional shareholders have sought greater independence between ADM's management and the board.
This followed a U.S. antitrust probe of the food and feed additives industry. Last year, ADM pleaded guilty to two counts of price-fixing and paid $100 million in fines.
